# Beyond Claude Code: The Anthropic Ecosystem for PMs

CEO at Product School

November 04, 2026 - 32 min read

The Anthropic ecosystem for AI product managers is a connected stack of AI tools that includes Claude Code, MCP, Claude Skills, sub-agents, the Anthropic API, Claude in Chrome, and Claude in Excel. Its real value comes from how these tools work together, not from what any single tool can do alone.

Claude Code is where many PMs start, for good reason. It is the most visible part of the stack because it produces the most tangible output: AI prototypes, specs, code changes, analysis, tests, and working artifacts.

But stopping at Claude Code is a little like buying a Leatherman and only using the knife. Useful, yes. But also a waste of the system.

If you haven’t read our case for why Claude Code matters for PMs, start with our guide. This piece is for PMs who are already familiar with Claude Code and acts as a map of how Claude Code, MCP, Skills, sub-agents, and more combine into PM workflows that no single tool produces on its own.

Because the PMs who get the biggest advantage from Anthropic will be the ones who know how to orchestrate the stack.

## Key Takeaways

The compounding value of Anthropic’s tools for PMs lives in the connections between Claude Code, MCP, Skills, sub-agents, the API, Chrome, and Excel.

Claude Code is the most visible entry point into the Anthropic stack, but it becomes more powerful when connected to live PM tools, reusable instructions, and specialized AI agents.

MCP turns Claude from a standalone assistant into part of the PM workflow by connecting it to tools like Linear, Jira, GitHub, Notion, Figma, Slack, and analytics platforms.

Claude Skills give PMs reusable operating playbooks for recurring work like PRDs, competitive analysis, release notes, research synthesis, and stakeholder updates.

The PM advantage is shifting from knowing how to prompt one AI tool to knowing how to design workflows across multiple AI capabilities.

## The Map: What’s Actually in the Anthropic Stack

The easiest mistake is to think of Anthropic as “Claude plus Claude Code.” That is true in the same way a product organization is “an AI plus engineers.” Technically correct. Strategically and rationally incomplete.

A better way to understand the Anthropic stack is by where each tool sits in the PM workflow. Some tools help you direct work. Some connect Claude to the systems where work already lives.

PM work rarely happens in one place. A single decision might touch a Jira ticket, a Figma file, and a stakeholder update. The stack becomes valuable when Claude can move across that environment with the right context, instructions, and permissions.

Here is the practical map.

Tool

What it does

Who it’s for

Where it fits in a PM workflow

---|---|---|---

Claude Code

Claude Code is Anthropic’s agentic coding tool that can read files, write code, run commands, and operate inside a real project environment.

PMs who want to move closer to prototypes, specs, implementation details, technical tradeoffs, and product artifacts.

It sits closest to building, debugging, prototyping, codebase exploration, and turning product intent into working output.

Anthropic API

The Anthropic API lets teams build Claude-powered experiences, internal tools, eval pipelines, and product features outside the Claude app.

PMs working with engineering on AI features, internal AI tools, model selection, or evaluation criteria.

It appears when AI becomes part of the product itself, not just part of the PM’s personal workflow.

Claude Skills

Claude Skills are reusable instruction bundles that Claude can load when a task requires a specific workflow, format, standard, or reference set.

PMs and product teams that repeat the same work often enough to turn it into a playbook.

They fit recurring workflows like PRDs, release notes, competitive analysis, customer synthesis, and stakeholder updates.

Model Context Protocol (MCP)

MCP is an open protocol that lets Claude and other AI tools connect to external systems through standardized adapters called MCP servers.

PMs whose work depends on live data from tools like Linear, Jira, GitHub, Notion, Figma, Slack, PostHog, Amplitude, or Google Drive.

It turns Claude from a standalone assistant into a workflow participant that can see and act on the systems PMs already use.

MCP servers

MCP servers expose specific tools, data sources, and actions to Claude through the Model Context Protocol.

Teams that want Claude to interact with product systems in a controlled and reusable way.

They sit between Claude and the PM stack, making live product context available without manual copy-paste.

Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome brings Claude into the browser so it can read pages, navigate websites, and help with web-based workflows.

PMs doing market research, competitive monitoring, vendor analysis, user research, and repetitive web workflows.

It fits the research layer of PM work, especially when useful context lives across web pages and SaaS tools.

Claude in Excel

Claude in Excel embeds Claude inside spreadsheets so users can ask questions, inspect formulas, update assumptions, and work across complex workbooks.

PMs working on pricing, usage analysis, forecasting, business cases, growth models, or spreadsheet-heavy planning.

It fits the analytical layer of PM work, where product decisions depend on models, scenarios, and tabular data.

Claude apps

Claude apps give PMs everyday access to Claude across chat, documents, files, and general knowledge work.

PMs who need a flexible workspace for thinking, drafting, synthesis, and analysis.

They act as the general-purpose surface for product thinking before the work moves into more specialized tools.

Sub-agents

Sub-agents are specialized Claude instances that Claude Code can delegate to for task-specific work with separate instructions and context windows.

PMs handling research-heavy, parallelizable, or multi-part workflows.

They fit orchestration work such as competitive teardowns, interview synthesis, backlog audits, and multi-area product analysis.

The key is not to memorize the tools. It is to see the layers.

Builder tools are where you direct the work: Claude Code, the Anthropic API, and Claude Skills.

Connector tools are where the work meets your existing systems: Model Context Protocol (MCP) and MCP servers.

Surface tools are where Claude shows up alongside other software: Claude in Chrome, Claude in Excel, and Claude apps.

Orchestration tools are where one Claude directs other specialized Claude instances: sub-agents.

Once you see the stack this way, the strategic question is about which layer of the PM workflow is currently the weakest?

If the problem is blank-page repetition, start with Skills. If the problem is copy-pasting context from product systems, look at MCP. If the problem is research spread across multiple sources, consider Chrome or sub-agents. If the problem is building or evaluating AI inside the product, the API enters the conversation.

## Claude Code’s Place in the Stack (and Why It Isn’t the Whole Stack)

Claude Code is Anthropic’s agentic coding tool. It reads files, writes code, runs commands, and operates inside a real project environment.

For many PMs, it is the first Anthropic tool that makes the future feel tangible, because it turns product thinking into something you can inspect: a prototype, a test, a spec, a pull request, a working artifact.

That is why we made the case for why Claude Code matters for product managers first. But I would not mistake the most visible tool for the whole system.

Anuj, Director of Product at Merge, captured the deeper issue well on the Product School Webinar: “Your agent is only as good as the data it has access to. An agent without data access is basically just expensive autocomplete.” That is exactly the shift PMs need to internalize.

In fact, Gartner’s 2025 research makes the same point at enterprise scale: 63% of organizations either do not have or are unsure whether they have the right data management practices for AI.

Gartner predicts that through 2026, organizations will abandon 60% of AI projects that are not supported by AI-ready data. In other words, this puts even bigger emphasis on the question of “what trusted context can Claude Code actually work with?”

Claude Code is the workshop, not the supply chain.

It can build the cabinet, but its real leverage comes when it knows the room dimensions from Figma, the customer complaints from Zendesk, the roadmap constraints from Jira, the metrics from Amplitude, etc.

## MCP — The Connector That Turns Claude Into Part of Your Workflow

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard from Anthropic that lets Claude and other AI tools connect to external systems through standardized adapters called MCP servers.

From a PM’s point of view, MCP solves one of the most frustrating problems in AI work: the model is smart, but blind. It can reason well and generate useful outputs. But unless it can see your Linear tickets, Jira backlog, Notion docs, or Google Drive folders, it is still working from whatever context you manually paste into the chat.

Anthropic describes MCP as a standard way for AI applications to receive context from external sources. They say it’s the “USB-C port for AI applications.” In Claude Code, MCP servers can give Claude access to external tools, databases, and APIs, including issue trackers, monitoring systems, design tools, and workflow apps.

Here is a simple version of what MCP unlocks:

Claude Code connects to Linear through an MCP server.

Claude pulls the open or completed tickets from the latest sprint.

The PM asks Claude to identify user-facing changes, skipped internal tasks, and risky ambiguity.

Claude drafts release notes from the actual ticket content.

Claude pushes the draft into Notion, where product marketing or customer success can review it.

# 挑战搜索巨头初见成效：OpenAI官方证实，ChatGPT搜索查询量已达谷歌的20%

11月4日消息，据国外媒体最新报道，人工智能巨头 OpenAI 挑战传统搜索巨头谷歌的进程已正式取得了突破性进展。在相关采访中，OpenAI 消费者产品负责人亚当·弗莱公开证实，目前 ChatGPT 平台上的搜索类查询量，已经达到了谷歌搜索查询量的20%。

回顾行业发展的大背景，皮尤研究中心今年夏天曾发布过一份详尽的调查报告。数据显示，“搜索信息”已经成为美国成年人最常见的人工智能使用场景，有高达42% 的受访者曾尝试用 AI 来检索和寻找信息;紧随其后的是工作用途，占比达到38%，主要用于处理各类职场任务;相比之下，娱乐消遣、获取新闻以及寻求医疗建议等则属于相对靠后的使用场景。

需要指出的是，该调查并非专门针对某一特定产品。不过，从市场渗透率来看，ChatGPT 在各大 AI 聊天机器人中依然占据绝对领先地位。统计显示，有44% 的受访美国成年人都曾使用过 ChatGPT，而排名第二的 Gemini 占比则为24%。

面对 AI 工具与传统搜索引擎日益激烈的竞争格局，谷歌母公司 Alphabet CEO 桑达尔·皮查伊此前在接受媒体采访时曾给出了自己的看法。他当时指出，尽管聊天机器人的用户规模已经达到了数亿级别，但谷歌自身的搜索查询量同样在保持增长，因此这远远谈不上是一场零和博弈。他曾以视频流媒体举例类比:“TikTok 出现后，大家都开始使用 TikTok，但 YouTube 在那段时间同样保持增长，而且表现非常出色。”

今日，OpenAI发布公告，宣布将于今年12月调整ChatGPT与Codex的使用额度规则。 根据新规，ChatGPT Plus、Pro和Business三大付费套餐的使用额度将合并计算，ChatGPT与Codex不再分别计算额度，而是共享同一额度池。 此次调整与OpenAI将ChatGPT Work的智能体能力整合进ChatGPT有关，旨在让用户能够直接在ChatGPT中完成更多复杂任务。 调整后，ChatGPT与Codex的额度消耗将统一按Token计算，具体消耗量

AI日报要点：OpenAI上线ChatGPT“锁定聊天”；蚂蚁开源Ming-3.0-tts登顶TTS评测；谷歌车载Gemini打通Gmail、日历、地图；Mistral发布Voxtral 3语音Agent SDK；Meta Muse 40天下载破千万；Spotify清理超5000万首AI垃圾歌；王腾ISHO Ring智能戒指将发；办公Agent前三为WorkBuddy、百度搭子、千问办公。

### AI Agent 搜索 Skill 推荐：搭一套 “统一入口 + 专项增强” 的搜索链路

文章梳理AI Agent联网搜索Skill选型，指出MCP成主流接入标准。核心思路是先分层再组合：以统一搜索入口打底，按需叠加网页精读、私有知识库、专业垂搜、并行检索与事实校验；对比AnySearch、Tavily、Brave、Exa、Firecrawl、Qdrant等适用场景，并给出轻量、生产级、企业内、深度调研等组合方案及避坑建议。

### 荐AI日报：百度升级AI搜索；豆包工作正式接入DeepSeek；谷歌Gemini全面支持PDF、表格等内联编辑

AI日报汇总：百度AI搜索升级、API低至4.9元/千次；豆包工作接入DeepSeek、Kimi、GLM；Gemini支持对话内编辑PDF/表格/代码；Kimi接入谷歌办公；豆包推30天免费订阅；Spotify拟推AI混音；Neuralink让Grok接入大脑；英伟达开源Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe，支持40语种转录、8人分离。

### OpenAI正式向全球ChatGPT用户推送GPT-6

OpenAI向全球ChatGPT用户推送GPT-6，取代GPT-5.6 Sol与Luna。新增智能UI，回答可生成图表、交互界面、计算器及小游戏，不再局限于文字。升级覆盖免费和付费用户：付费用户用GPT-6 Sol，免费及Go用户用GPT-6 Luna。GPT-6支持边思考边输出，联网搜索等待缩短44%，并提升搜索质量与安全性。

### AI Agent 搜索 MCP 推荐：AnySearch，给智能体一个可信的搜索入口

AI Agent正从模型比拼转向落地应用，信息获取成为关键。AnySearch作为AI时代的搜索基础设施，通过MCP协议为Agent提供结构化、可追溯的搜索结果，覆盖金融、学术、代码等二十余类垂直领域，准确率达76.4%。已接入20万开发者，API调用超2000万次，免费开放，每日1000次额度。

### 亮相Aquatech China 2026，安吉尔凭借领先科技荣膺两项水技术创新奖

OpenAI.content:
Advertisement

# OpenAI fails to block Singapore startup's 'GemGPT' trademark

OpenAI has lost its bid to stop Singapore startup Porolis Technologies from registering the trademark "GemGPT", after a tribunal found that sharing the letters "GPT" alone was insufficient to prove consumer confusion.

In a decision on 28 October, the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) dismissed all five grounds of opposition filed by OpenAI, allowing Porolis' application to proceed. OpenAI was ordered to pay SG$10,000 in costs.

Advertisement

The dispute centred on whether "GPT" is seen by Singapore consumers as a distinctive identifier for OpenAI, or as a generic technical term for generative AI.

Porolis, part of the BP de Silva group, develops AI tools to assess gemstone grading, authenticity and treatment. It argued that "Gem" referred to its focus on gemstones and "GPT" described its own generative pre-trained transformer models built in-house, without using OpenAI's technology.

OpenAI argued that GemGPT conflicted with its existing marks, including CHATGPT, GPT-3 and GPT-4. However, the tribunal noted that OpenAI does not hold an earlier standalone registration for "GPT" itself.

Principal Assistant Registrar Gabriel Ong acknowledged ChatGPT's rapid adoption in Singapore, noting almost 11 million monthly visits to OpenAI's site from the country by May 2023. But he found that familiarity with ChatGPT did not mean consumers view "GPT" in isolation as identifying OpenAI. He also noted "GPT" was already used as technical terminology among AI researchers before ChatGPT launched.

Comparing the marks, Ong found CHATGPT and GemGPT to be similar only to a marginal degree, with the overall impression being that GemGPT relates to an unrelated AI service for gemstones.

Advertisement

On bad faith, OpenAI argued Porolis filed for GemGPT less than six months after ChatGPT's launch to ride on its reputation. While Ong accepted Porolis would have known of OpenAI, he ruled that knowledge alone did not establish bad faith.

He added that the decision does not mean "GPT" can never become distinctive of OpenAI, with different evidence in future potentially leading to a different outcome. The ruling comes as OpenAI deepens its presence in Singapore. It established its APAC hub in Singapore in October 2024, at the time one of its highest per-capita markets for ChatGPT.

In May 2026, it committed over SG$300 million through a partnership with the Ministry of Digital Development and Information to set up its first Applied AI Lab outside the US, creating over 200 technical roles and supporting AI deployment across public services, finance and healthcare.

Google.content:
# Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with advanced cybersecurity features.

Although Gemini 4 Argon was only launched two weeks ago, Google says Carbon is now their highest-rated AI model.

The pace at which AI companies release new, advanced models has accelerated dramatically in recent months, as leading AI labs race to acquire the best models available.

Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra earlier that month, and Google announced Argon on September 30 before releasing it to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers on October 13.

Each lab claimed the lead within just weeks of the previous version. Much like Argon, Google announced Carbon relatively early, before most people could use it.

The early release allows Google to take the lead in the rankings right now. It also allows people to review the standards before the next release round takes place.

The new model achieved the top position on the updated Artificial Intelligence Analysis Index v5.0 with a score of 59. Carbon demonstrated improvements in programming tasks and automated agents, achieving 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability discovery, 54.8% on ExploitGym for vulnerability exploitation, and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching.

Google says Carbon uses the same safety system as Argon, including monitoring the model's inference process and adding work on alignment, or keeping the model functioning as intended. According to Google's own testing, Carbon also performs better than its predecessor.

You may also like

Google stated that Carbon never successfully cheated on Terminal-Bench 4.0, meaning it never found a shortcut to complete a task without actually doing the work, and it only attempted to cheat 0.4% of the time.

During internal programming, serious misdirection warnings—signaling the model behaving in ways developers didn't expect—were reduced by nearly 80%. Carbon also delivered about half the number of unsupported requests compared to Argon.

And on the Gray Swan benchmark test for prompt injection, which checks whether hidden commands can hijack the model, Carbon blocked all attack attempts, improving Argon's attack success rate by 0.7%.

Currently, Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Google-approved cybersecurity professionals in the Fairwind Program. Starting this week, Carbon is being rolled out to a small group of testers, and Google says it will gradually add more trusted partners.

Developers, businesses, and consumers will have access later, but Google has not yet given an official public launch date.

If we use Argon as a time estimate, approximately two weeks have passed from the announcement of this feature to its appearance in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra users. However, we cannot confirm whether Google is committed to a similar timeline for Carbon.

You may also like

When Carbon is integrated into the API, Google says its price will be equivalent to Argon's launch price: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Input tokens are cached at a 95% discount to the input price.

This helps Carbon maintain a significantly lower price compared to its main competitors. Previously, Mashable reported that Claude Opus 5.5 was priced at $4 per million tokens in and $20 per million tokens out, while GPT-6 Astra was priced at $10 per million tokens in and $50 per million tokens out.

# feat(models): Support Gemini 4 Carbon for Enterprise Gemini CLI users #30125

## Description

### What would you like to be added?

We would like official support for Google's newest flagship model, Gemini 4 Carbon (announced October 28, 2026), in Gemini CLI for users authenticated via Gemini Code Assist Enterprise / Standard (OAuth) and Gemini API Keys.

Specifically, this includes:

- Model ID Registration: Addinggemini-4-carbon (and relevant aliases/variants) to VALID_GEMINI_MODELS in packages/core/src/config/models.ts.
- Model Configurations: Defining model configuration (family, tier, thinking levels, tool capabilities) inpackages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts.
- Model Picker UI: Adding the model to the/model selector dialog (packages/cli/src/ui/components/ModelDialog.tsx).
- Schema Update: Updatingschemas/settings.schema.json to allow configuration and validation.
- Backend Coordination: Enabling the corresponding model routing/entitlements in the Gemini Code Assist backend (cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com / Vertex AI enterprise endpoints).

### Why is this needed?

State-of-the-Art Agentic & Coding Capabilities:

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, 2026, specifically optimized for complex reasoning, long-horizon agentic workflows, and end-to-end software engineering & security repair. As Gemini CLI is designed for autonomous terminal software engineering, Gemini 4 Carbon is the ideal flagship foundation model for these workflows.

Widening Gap for Enterprise Users (Ref feat(models): Support Gemini 4 Argon / Gemini 4 Pro for Enterprise Gemini CLI users #29689):

In feat(models): Support Gemini 4 Argon / Gemini 4 Pro for Enterprise Gemini CLI users #29689, we requested support for Gemini 4 Argon. While Argon is still pending enablement in Code Assist Enterprise, the frontier landscape has moved forward with Carbon. Enterprise users remain capped on older Pro models (such asgemini-3.1-pro-preview), creating a widening capability gap between early preview channels and licensed enterprise environments.

Enterprise Commitment & InfoSec Constraints:

During the migration announcement on May 19, 2026, Google affirmed:
"If your organization uses Gemini CLI or our IDE extensions via a Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise license, your access remains unchanged. We’ll continue to support Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist with access to the latest Gemini models and other updates."

Many regulated enterprise organizations have strict InfoSec review and compliance constraints that prevent deploying newer preview tools (like Antigravity CLI) until comprehensive vendor security assessments conclude. Gemini CLI remains the primary approved, enterprise-compliant terminal agent for these teams.

### Additional context

- Reference Issue: feat(models): Support Gemini 4 Argon / Gemini 4 Pro for Enterprise Gemini CLI users #29689 (Support Gemini 4 Argon / Gemini 4 Pro for Enterprise Gemini CLI users)
- Auth Method: Gemini Code Assist Enterprise (Google OAuth) andgemini-api-key.
- Key Implementation Files:
- packages/core/src/config/models.ts
- packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts
- packages/cli/src/ui/components/ModelDialog.tsx
- schemas/settings.schema.json

We understand that Gemini 4 Carbon is beginning with gated/safety evaluations (e.g., Fairwind Program) before broader general availability. We kindly ask the Gemini CLI and Code Assist teams to plan for Carbon's integration and backend routing so Enterprise users can leverage it as availability opens up.

Google.content:
# Red Heart Shapes Influence AI Code Generation: New Google DeepMind Study

# Red Heart Shapes Influence AI Code Generation: New Google DeepMind Study
so interesting. 🤔
New Google DeepMind and Stanford paper finds that a red heart picture in the prompt can decide how AI write code, that simple shapes in images can steer AI on unrelated tasks, often without the models saying so.
plain colored shapes in a prompt change how AI models write code, though the shapes have nothing to do with it.
Vision-language models now read screenshots and images as part of normal work. If an unrelated picture changes the model's choice, builders need to see it, ideally in the model's own reasoning.
They added a plain colored shape, like a red heart, to a coding prompt and told the model to look at it. Across 288 shapes, they tracked how often Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 chose recursion.
A red heart moved Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.4 from 0% recursive solutions to 100% on a binary tree problem. When a shape did steer Gemini 3.1 Pro, 71.5% of its thinking traces called the image irrelevant.
If your agent sees images, test its decisions with and without them, and do not count on reasoning traces to flag visual influence.
# A Heart Means Recursion: Exploring Visual Meaning and Communication in VLMs

Alexa Tartaglini\({}^{1,2}\), Zhengyuan Wu\({}^{1}\), Thaddäus Wiedemer\({}^{1}\), Martin Wattenberg\({}^{1}\), Been Kim\({}^{1}\) and Yuxuan Li\({}^{1}\)

\({}^{1}\)Google DeepMind, \({}^{2}\)Stanford University. Work done as a Student Researcher at Google DeepMind.

###### Abstract

Do vision-language models (VLMs) share our ability to communicate visually? We share preliminary findings, starting from a surprising observation: simple visual symbols like a red heart can strongly influence model behavior on seemingly unrelated tasks, such as steering models towards recursive solutions on simple coding problems. Notably, this steering effect is largely implicit, as models' direct interpretations and thinking traces about visual symbols diverge substantially from their observed behavior. In visual communication between models, this leads to a generation-interpretation gap: while models tend to send shape primitives that they (and humans) find intuitive, these visual cues often fail to steer other models. In further communication games involving abstract concepts and stories, models can creatively use visuals to transmit meaning to one another, although some communications remain non-intuitive to humans. These findings reveal that VLMs might be capable of rich, creative, and visually-grounded communication, but their interpretation and production of visual meaning diverges from human conventions in surprising ways. Together this work highlights both the promise and challenges of visual communication between humans and VLMs.

### Summary

Research from Google DeepMind and Stanford demonstrates that vision-language models can be influenced by unrelated visual shapes in coding prompts. The study tested 288 shapes across Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, finding that a red heart image increased recursive solutions from 0% to 100% for Claude and GPT. Remarkably, 71.5% of Gemini's reasoning traces deemed the image irrelevant yet still showed shape-induced behavior, suggesting visual influence may occur without model awareness.

# Google AI Updates: November 4, 2026

## 1. Gemini API Deprecates Gemini 2.5 Pro and 2.5 Flash, Auto-Routing Both to Newer Flash Models on December 1

Google deprecatedgemini-2.5-pro and gemini-2.5-flash in the Gemini API on November 2, and neither can be selected in Google AI Studio any longer. From December 1, 2026, every API request to gemini-2.5-pro will be routed automatically to gemini-3.8-flash and billed at Gemini 3.8 Flash rates, and requests to gemini-2.5-flash will be routed to gemini-3.5-flash-lite and billed at Flash-Lite rates. Google lists breaking API changes for both migrations: changes to function calling and thought_signature validation, thinking_level replacing thinking_budget, and the removal of sampling parameters and prefilled model turns, so applications that still set a thinking budget, pass sampling parameters or prefill an assistant turn need code changes, not just a new model string, before the cutover. Source

## 2. Google Releases Physical-Engineering’s Last Exam, an 85-Task Agent Benchmark Where No Model Reaches 50%

Google’s AI & Infrastructure team, working with Mercor, announced Physical-Engineering’s Last Exam (PLE), a benchmark and open competition for agents doing mechanical (30 tasks), electrical (27), civil (18) and structural (10) engineering work. Each of the 85 long-horizon tasks runs in a containerized project folder built on Mercor’s Archipelago environment with an average of 61 files (5,170 in total) such as PDFs, spreadsheets, emails, 2D CAD drawings, 3D BIM models and document revisions, and the agent must find the governing codes and physical limits, run calculations and produce deliverables a licensed reviewer would sign off; 44 tasks were written by practicing engineers and 41 were assembled by an agent pipeline from engineer-designed specs, then validated and made harder by engineers. Points are awarded only if a design passes every hard safety check: the top configuration met 91% of individual constraints on co-authored tasks, but only 41.3% of its deliverables passed every hard safety and feasibility check, and model choice mattered far more than harness (up to a 50-point spread across models against a median 3-point spread across harnesses for the same model). On the leaderboard at ple-bench.com, which scores each model on its native harness at maximum reasoning over the 56 hidden tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code leads at 0.483, followed by GPT-6 Astra in Codex (0.458), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (0.435) and Google’s Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity (0.406), with Grok 4.7 at 0.301; Gemini 4 Carbon is not listed. Google released 29 public tasks, grading scripts and the evaluation container on GitHub, a paper on arXiv, and a submission process for the private set, with 13 Google-sponsored models running free on its servers and prize details still to come. Source

## 3. Google Makes Gemini and Search Opt-In for K-12 Student Accounts, and Schools That Refuse AI Lose Search Entirely

Google announced at its AI in the Learning Era event on November 3 that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on, with specifics to be shared with schools “in the coming months” before the change rolls out (TechCrunch reports it is planned for next year). Because AI features are built into Search, education VP Chris Phillips told The New York Times that schools restricting AI altogether “will not have access to search,” and students will see a message from their school instead. Alongside the controls, Guided Learning, the Gemini study mode that coaches with step-by-step prompts instead of final answers, is rolling out globally in Google Classroom as teacher-assigned activities anchored on uploaded course material, with insights showing teachers how students engaged, and is coming to Search for student accounts through a pilot in select U.S. schools later this month. Google also published a randomized controlled trial with more than 300 University of Tokyo students in which half a day of statistics study with Guided Learning raised test scores by 8.1 percentage points against 5.3 points with standard web resources alone, plus a four-week pilot with Ark across three UK secondary schools, and announced Google.org funding for five organizations building AI tools for teachers. Source Research TechCrunch

## 4. Google DeepMind Adds Cheminformatics Skills to Antigravity’s Science Plugin

Google DeepMind released Cheminformatics Skills for Google Antigravity, available now by installing the Science plugin in the Antigravity app, and for enterprise users who sign in with Google Cloud credentials. The skills split the work so the language model handles orchestration, database navigation and scientific reasoning while deterministic tools grounded in the open-source RDKit toolkit run the molecular calculations, with connectors to ChEMBL and PubChem. In a walkthrough built on the lung cancer drugs crizotinib and its cyclized successor lorlatinib, the agent pulled thousands of compounds from the literature, filtered out buffers and solvents, ran matched molecular pair analysis, trained and validated potency models (using chronological splits where dates exist, otherwise scaffold splits) across four experimental readouts, and proposed new rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes and electron-pushing diagrams in about an hour, a workflow DeepMind says typically takes multiple days; results export to standard chemistry software formats and can be prepared for AlphaFold or molecular dynamics. DeepMind cautions that sparse data, inter-lab assay noise and narrow dynamic ranges limit predictive precision and that every proposed design still has to be synthesized and tested. Source

Meta.content:
Meta Muse 推出 AI Agent 应用软件和开放权重模型

关键要点

Meta 于 2026 年 9 月 8 日在美国推出 Muse 个人 AI Agent 应用，可用于浏览网页、填写表单、发送邮件和预订旅行。

据第三方定价追踪器称，通过 Meta Model API 使用 Muse Spark 1.3，每百万个输入代币约需 1.25 美元，每百万个输出代币约需 4.25 美元。

Muse Glimmer 是一款采用 Apache 2.0 许可证的 30B 开放权重模型，可在配备 24-32 GB 内存的消费级 GPU 或 Mac 设备上运行。

Meta 于 2026 年 9 月 8 日在美国推出了 Muse 个人 AI Agent 应用。该应用可以浏览网页、填写表单、发送邮件并为用户预订服务。Meta Superintelligence Labs 也将 Muse 这个名称用于多个模型，包括 Muse Spark、Muse Image、Muse Glimmer、Muse Spark Open 和 Muse Wonder。这一产品线取代了 Llama，成为 Meta 较新的模型系列，同时将 Meta AI 扩展至该公司的各款应用和开发者平台。

Meta Muse 将 AI Agent 应用与新模型相结合

Meta 于 2025 年将其 AI 工作整合到 Meta Superintelligence Labs，由首席 AI 主管 Alexandr Wang 领导。该团队将 Muse 用作其 AI 产品的品牌，而马克·扎克伯格将目标描述为“个人超级智能”：一种了解用户并为其采取行动的 AI。

Muse 产品栈包括 Muse 模型、面向开发者的 Meta Model API、Meta 各款应用中的 Meta AI、Muse 个人 Agent 应用以及 Muse Code。Muse 也与 WhatsApp、Instagram、Facebook 和 Meta 眼镜相连。Meta AI 此前运行于 Llama 模型，而如今由 Muse Spark 提供支持。Llama 仍是 Meta 较早推出的开放模型系列，Muse 则是 Meta Superintelligence Labs 推出的较新模型系列。

Muse 应用可运行长期个人任务

Meta 将 Muse 定位为可处理长期任务的 Agent，而非一次只回答一个问题的聊天机器人。它可以打开浏览器、填写表单，并代表用户进行协商。该应用可以发送邮件、预订旅行、管理日程、协助购物，并将长期目标转化为计划，例如为期一年的健身计划或创办小型企业的步骤。

即使关闭应用，任务也会继续运行，用户可以在 Agent 工作时观看其浏览器。每位用户的 Agent 都运行在 Meta 云端专属的虚拟机上。Meta 表示，该机器同时存放 Agent 和用户数据，其他用户的 Agent 无法访问。报道称，权限系统会控制 Agent 可以访问哪些服务，并将读取权限与写入权限分开。

该应用仅面向美国年满 18 岁的成年人开放。它支持 iOS、Android 和网页，还提供 Mac 客户端并集成到 WhatsApp 中。Muse 提供免费套餐，以及每月 20 美元和 100 美元的付费计划。Meta 表示，Muse 中没有广告。Muse Image 在 Meta AI、WhatsApp 和 Instagram Stories 中免费提供。

报道称，默认情况下，用户的查询会用于模型训练，但用户可以关闭这一选项。在 API 中，Standard 模式表示内容不会用于训练 Meta 的模型，而 Contributor 模式允许将内容用于训练，以换取更低的价格。

Muse 模型新增推理、图像、编程和 Agent 功能

Muse Spark 是一款为 Meta AI 提供支持的多模态推理模型。它设有 Instant 和 Thinking 模式，并能针对复杂问题并行启动多个子 Agent。它可以处理图像、健康问题、语音、可视化编程、Facebook Marketplace 和网页上的购物搜索，以及其他基于聊天的任务。

通过 API，Muse Spark 的上下文窗口为 1,048,576 个代币，并接受文本、图像、视频、音频和 PDF 输入。该模型可通过 Meta AI 应用、meta.ai，以及 WhatsApp、Instagram、Facebook 和 Messenger 中的 Meta AI 使用。

Muse Image 支持根据复杂提示词进行文生图，并可通过日常语言指令编辑图像。用户可以圈出或标记某个区域，只修改该部分；在 Meta AI 保留上下文的情况下逐步优化图像；还可以利用参考图编辑多张图像。Muse Image 还可以通过 @mentions 引入 Instagram 上的公开内容，并为创作者提供控制选项，同时为 Instagram Stories 中的 30 多种 AI 特效提供支持。

Muse Wonder 面向 Agent 工作负载。其 Active Memory 会在多轮对话中保留有关用户的重要上下文，并将相关细节带入当前任务。其 Active Focus 会持续推动模型实现困难目标；遇到阻碍时尝试其他方法，在需要时请求澄清，并在执行重要操作前征求确认。Muse Wonder 以 muse-wonder-1.0 的形式在 Meta Model API 上提供预览版，而 Muse Wonder Full 仅限更高级别的 Muse Code 订阅计划使用。

Muse Glimmer 是一款 30B 开放权重模型，适用于本地 Agent。它可以在一块消费级 GPU 上运行，也可以在配备约 24 到 32 GB 内存的 Mac 上以 4 位精度运行，并采用 Apache 2.0 许可证。Muse Spark Open 是 Muse Spark 的 8160 亿参数开放权重版本，总参数量为 8160 亿，在混合专家架构中有 420 亿活跃参数。它需要数据中心 GPU，或两台使用 MLX 的 512 GB Mac Studio，并采用带有限商业条款的 Muse Model License。

Meta Model API 提供 Muse 开发者访问权限

Meta Model API 使用基础 URL https://api.meta.ai/v1，并通过 bearer API 密钥进行身份验证。它支持适用于 Muse Spark 和 Muse Wonder 的 Chat Completions、Responses 和 Messages 风格请求，也支持 Muse Image 的图像生成和编辑端点。

模型 ID 包括：适用于新项目且使用 Standard 模式的 muse-spark-1.3；价格更低但允许将内容用于训练 Meta 模型的 muse-spark-1.3-contributor；仅以预览版和 Standard 模式提供的 muse-wonder-1.0；用于图像生成和编辑的 muse-image-1.0；以及用于语音转文本的 muse-voice-transcribe-1.0。

第三方定价追踪网站列出的 Muse Spark 1.3 价格约为每 100 万个输入代币 1.25 美元、每 100 万个输出代币 4.25 美元。据报道，新账户可获得免费额度。在为 API 使用制定预算前，应查看 Meta 的定价页面以确认最新价格。

Meta Muse 面临地区、数据和许可限制

Muse Agent 应用仅面向美国成年人开放，而 API 中的模型可用性因国家或地区而异。Muse Wonder 不在韩国提供。由 Muse Spark 提供支持的 Meta AI，其覆盖范围比 Agent 应用更广。

报道称，亚马逊于 2026 年 9 月 21 日封锁了 Muse 对其零售网站的访问，原因是该 Agent 没有表明自己的身份。Meta 表示，Muse 无法查看密码或支付方式。404 Media 还报道称，部分 Beta 版电话由人工呼叫中心员工接听，Meta 将其描述为标准的内部测试。

Muse Spark、Muse Wonder 和 Muse Image 均为闭源模型。Muse Spark Open 提供可下载的权重，但使用 Meta 自有的、附带有限商业条款的许可证。Muse Glimmer 是 Muse 系列中唯一被确定采用 Apache 2.0 许可证的模型。

Meta Muse 信息与访问详情

Muse 于 2026 年 9 月 8 日在美国推出。

Muse 提供免费套餐，以及每月 20 美元和 100 美元的付费计划。

通过 API，Muse Spark 的上下文窗口为 1,048,576 个代币。

Muse Image 为 Instagram Stories 中 30 多种 AI 特效提供支持。

Muse Wonder 以 muse-wonder-1.0 的形式在 Meta Model API 上提供预览版。

Muse Glimmer 是一款采用 Apache 2.0 许可证的 30B 开放权重模型。

Muse Spark Open 总参数量为 8160 亿，活跃参数量为 420 亿。

Muse Spark Open 可在两台使用 MLX 的 512 GB Mac Studio 上运行。

什么是 Meta Muse？

Meta Muse 是 Meta 为其个人 AI Agent 应用及由 Meta Superintelligence Labs 构建的较新 AI 模型系列所使用的名称。该应用可以浏览网页、填写表单、发送邮件并预订服务，而模型系列包括 Muse Spark、Muse Image、Muse Glimmer、Muse Spark Open 和 Muse Wonder。

Muse 与 Llama 有什么关系？

Llama 是 Meta 较早推出的开放模型系列。Muse 是 Meta Superintelligence Labs 推出的较新模型系列，而过去运行于 Llama 模型的 Meta AI，如今由 Muse Spark 提供支持。

开发者或用户可以自行运行哪些 Muse 模型？

Muse Glimmer 和 Muse Spark Open 是 Hugging Face 上提供的开放权重模型。Muse Glimmer 采用 Apache 2.0 许可证，可在一块消费级 GPU 上运行，也可以在配备约 24 到 32 GB 内存的 Mac 上以 4 位精度运行。Muse Spark Open 总参数量为 8160 亿，活跃参数量为 420 亿，需要数据中心 GPU，或两台使用 MLX 的 512 GB Mac Studio。

# Llama Guard

Llama Guard

AI model

Developer | Meta 
---|---
Released | December 2023 
Parameters | 1B, 8B, 11B, 12B 
Modalities | Text, Vision 
License | Llama Community License 
Access | Open weights 
Predecessor | LLaMA 

Llama Guard is a family of large language model-based safety classifiers developed by Meta AI as part of the PurpleLlama project for detecting unsafe content in human-AI conversations. First introduced in December 2023, Llama Guard was designed to function as an input-output safeguard that classifies both user prompts and AI-generated responses according to a structured safety risk taxonomy. The model was fine-tuned from LLaMA 2 and demonstrated that general-purpose language models could be repurposed as effective content moderation classifiers by framing safety evaluation as an instruction-following task. Across successive generations, Llama Guard expanded from a text-only English classifier built on a seven-billion-parameter base into a natively multimodal twelve-billion-parameter system capable of evaluating text and images simultaneously in multiple languages. The family includes Llama Guard (December 2023), Llama Guard 2 (April 2024), Llama Guard 3 (July 2024, with text, vision, and quantized variants), and Llama Guard 4 (April 2025), each aligned to progressively more comprehensive safety taxonomies and built on the corresponding generation of the LLaMA model series. Released under permissive open licenses and integrated into Meta's broader Llama Protections safety suite alongside LlamaFirewall, Prompt Guard, and Code Shield, Llama Guard has become one of the most widely deployed open-source safety classifiers in the artificial intelligence industry, adopted by cloud providers, inference platforms, and independent developers as a standardized content moderation layer for generative AI applications.

## Background and development

The development of Llama Guard arose from a growing recognition within the AI research community that deploying large language models in consumer-facing applications required systematic, scalable approaches to content safety that went beyond simple keyword filtering or rule-based moderation. By 2023, the proliferation of conversational AI assistants had made it clear that both user inputs and model outputs could contain harmful content spanning categories such as violence, self-harm, sexual material, criminal planning, and regulated substances. Existing moderation tools, including the OpenAI Moderation API and various toxicity classifiers, relied on fixed taxonomies and opaque, non-customizable architectures that could not easily adapt to the evolving safety requirements of different deployment contexts. Researchers at Meta recognized that the same instruction-following capabilities that made large language models effective at general tasks could be redirected toward safety classification, producing a moderation system that was both transparent and adaptable.

The original Llama Guard paper, authored by Hakan Inan, Kartikeyi Upasani, Jianfeng Chi, Rashi Rungta, Krithika Iyer, Yuning Mao, Michael Tontchev, Qing Hu, Brian Fuller, Davide Testuggine, and Madian Khabsa at Meta, was released on December 7, 2023, on the arXiv preprint server. The paper introduced both a safety risk taxonomy for human-AI interactions and the Llama Guard model itself, which was fine-tuned from the instruction-tuned variant of LLaMA 2 at the seven-billion-parameter scale. The key insight driving the design was that by including the safety taxonomy directly in the model's input prompt, the classifier could be taught to reason about policy violations in a structured way, and different taxonomies could be swapped in at inference time without retraining. This made Llama Guard fundamentally different from earlier moderation APIs that embedded their policies as fixed, hidden components of the model's training objective.

The original safety risk taxonomy defined six categories for evaluating content: violence and hate, sexual content, guns and illegal weapons, regulated or controlled substances, criminal planning, and suicide and self-harm. These categories were inspired by existing taxonomies from major AI companies including Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI, but were designed to be openly published and modifiable. The taxonomy was deliberately kept concise to serve as a demonstration of the instruction-tuned classification approach, with the understanding that deployers would customize it for their specific applications. Each category included detailed definitions and examples that were formatted as part of the input prompt, allowing the model to ground its classification decisions in explicit policy language rather than implicit patterns learned during pretraining.

Llama Guard was released as a component of the PurpleLlama project, Meta's umbrella initiative for open-source AI safety tools. The name "Purple Llama" drew from the cybersecurity concept of purple teaming, which combines offensive security testing (red teaming) with defensive security measures (blue teaming) into a unified approach. Alongside Llama Guard, the initial PurpleLlama release included CyberSecEval, a benchmark suite for evaluating the cybersecurity risks of code generated by language models. The decision to release these tools openly reflected Meta's broader strategy of positioning its Llama model family as the leading open-source AI ecosystem, where safety tooling would be as freely available as the models themselves. This approach stood in contrast to proprietary safety systems offered by competitors such as OpenAI and Google, whose moderation tools were accessible only through paid APIs.

The evolution of Llama Guard across subsequent generations tracked closely with the development of the LLaMA model family itself. Llama Guard 2, released in April 2024, was rebuilt on the LLaMA 3 architecture at the eight-billion-parameter scale and adopted the MLCommons standardized hazard taxonomy, a collaborative industry effort to define a common set of safety categories. This shift from Meta's proprietary taxonomy to an industry standard was significant, as it positioned Llama Guard as a reference implementation for the emerging consensus on AI safety classification rather than a single company's interpretation of what constituted harmful content. The MLCommons taxonomy expanded the original six categories to eleven, covering a broader range of harms including defamation, privacy violations, intellectual property concerns, and specialized advice in domains such as medicine, law, and finance.

Llama Guard 3, released alongside LLaMA 3.1 in July 2024, represented a substantial expansion of the family's capabilities. Rather than a single model, Llama Guard 3 comprised three variants: an eight-billion-parameter text classifier aligned to the updated MLCommons taxonomy of thirteen hazard categories plus a fourteenth category for code interpreter abuse, an eleven-billion-parameter vision model capable of classifying multimodal prompts containing both text and images, and a one-billion-parameter model designed for lightweight deployment scenarios. The text variant supported content moderation in eight languages beyond English, addressing a critical gap in earlier versions that had been limited to English-language content. The vision variant, built on the LLaMA 3.2 eleven-billion-parameter vision architecture, represented the first extension of the Llama Guard approach to image understanding, enabling safety classification of prompts that combined textual instructions with visual content.

Llama Guard 4, released in April 2025 alongside LLaMA 4, consolidated the text and vision capabilities into a single natively multimodal model with twelve billion parameters. Where Llama Guard 3 had required separate models for text-only and text-plus-image classification, Llama Guard 4 handled both modalities within a unified architecture. The model was derived from the Llama 4 Scout pretrained model through a process of architectural pruning that removed the mixture-of-experts routing layers, retaining only the shared expert to produce a dense feedforward network suitable for the binary classification task of safety evaluation. This pruning-then-fine-tuning approach reflected a broader trend in the field toward deriving specialized task-specific models from large general-purpose pretrained models rather than training classifiers from scratch.

## Architecture

The architectural design of the Llama Guard family is built on the principle that a transformer-based language model can serve as an effective safety classifier when the classification task is framed as an instruction-following problem. Rather than modifying the underlying model architecture with custom classification heads or specialized output layers, Llama Guard uses the standard autoregressive text generation mechanism of its base model to produce structured classification outputs. The model receives a formatted prompt containing the safety taxonomy, the content to be evaluated, and an instruction specifying whether the content is a user prompt or an AI response, and it generates a textual output indicating whether the content is safe or unsafe, along with the specific violated category if applicable.

The original Llama Guard was built on the Llama 2-7B instruction-tuned architecture, inheriting the standard transformer decoder design with grouped-query attention, rotary positional embeddings, SwiGLU activation functions, and root-mean-square layer normalization. The model's vocabulary and tokenizer were identical to those of the base Llama 2 model, and no architectural modifications were made to the transformer layers themselves. Meta.content:

# A Ryzen AI NPU Build of Llama 3.1 8B Lands on Modelers.cn with 16K Context

Modelers.cn is best known as a Huawei/Ascend-oriented hub, so an AMD-targeted Llama release is a genuinely interesting sight. amd/Llama-3.1-8Brai1.7.1npu16K is a repackaged build of Meta’s Llama 3.1…

Modelers.cn is best known as a Huawei/Ascend-oriented hub, so an AMD-targeted Llama release is a genuinely interesting sight.amd/Llama-3.1-8B_rai_1.7.1_npu_16K is a repackaged build of Meta’s Llama 3.1 8B text-generation model, converted with AMD’s RAI (Ryzen AI) toolchain v1.7.1 for a 16K-context variant aimed at Ryzen AI NPUs. For developers with Copilot+-class laptops or mini-PCs, the appeal is straightforward: a well-known 8B Llama checkpoint in a form that the Ryzen AI stack can execute directly on the integrated NPU, enabling low-power local chat and text generation. You can grab it in one line from Modelers.cn: git clone https://modelers.cn/amd/Llama-3.1-8B_rai_1.7.1_npu_16K.git.

The goal here is to provide Llama 3.1 8B in a form AMD’s Ryzen AI toolchain can run directly on the integrated NPU at a 16K context length. That context window is a useful step up from the 4K/8K configurations often shipped in NPU demos, and the 8B parameter count keeps download size and memory pressure reasonable for client devices. The Llama 3.1 community licence permits commercial use, subject to the usual 700 million monthly-active-user caveat. What makes it notable is less the base model — Llama 3.1 8B is familiar territory — than the packaging: an NPU-ready Ryzen AI artefact on an Ascend-centric platform. No Ascend NPU support is stated here, so readers looking for Huawei hardware support should not assume it.

That said, the listing is a bare stub: there is no model card body, no usage instructions, no conversion script, no quantisation format, no benchmarks, and no software prerequisites. We cannot verify whatrai_1.7.1 implies in practice — whether the precision is INT4, INT8 or W4ABF16, what the ONNX layout is, or which driver and runtime versions are required. Llama 3.1 8B is also an older base model now; newer small models from Qwen, Llama 3.3 and others generally outperform it at similar size. There is no safety, bias or quality evaluation for this specific converted build, and it is a single-format artefact with no GGUF or other fallback for CPU/GPU users. In short: worth a look if you already have a Ryzen AI NPU and want a known Llama checkpoint for local inference, but treat it as an experiment until AMD and Modelers.cn publish the missing details.

## Strengths

- Makes a well-known 8B Llama 3.1 checkpoint available for NPU execution, enabling low-power, local inference on Copilot+-class laptops.
- 16K context window is a useful step up from the 4K/8K configurations often shipped in NPU demos.
- Small parameter count keeps download size and memory pressure reasonable for client devices.
- Llama 3.1 community licence permits commercial use, with the usual 700M monthly-active-user caveat.

## Limitations

- The model card has no body at all — no usage instructions, conversion script, quantisation format, benchmarks or software prerequisites.
- Cannot verify whatrai_1.7.1 implies: precision (INT4/INT8/W4ABF16), ONNX layout, or required driver and runtime versions are all unstated.
- Targets AMD Ryzen AI NPUs, which is inconsistent with Modelers.cn’s Ascend-centric audience and may confuse readers looking for Huawei hardware support.
- Llama 3.1 8B is now an older base model; newer small models from Qwen, Llama 3.3 and others generally outperform it at similar size.
- No safety, bias or quality evaluation is provided for this specific converted build.
- Single-format artefact with no GGUF or other fallback for CPU/GPU users.

View the full model page at https://aichina.news/models/amd/Llama-3.1-8B_rai_1.7.1_npu_16K/

Meta.content:
# 半年一颗芯：Meta把自研AI芯片节奏压到英伟达三分之一，赌的是"推理优先"

据路透社11月3日报道，Meta披露了自研AI芯片MTIA的新路线图：两年内连推四代（MTIA 300/400/450/500），工作负载从排名推荐训练一路覆盖到生成式AI推理，发布节奏压缩到约每半年一颗。Meta官方博客称，从300到500代，HBM带宽累计提升4.5倍、算力提升约25倍。几乎同期，据澎湃等媒体，Meta将与其芯片合作方博通（Broadcom）的定制协议续签至2029年，初始算力承诺即超1GW，博通CEO陈福阳退出董事会转任顾问，盘后股价涨约3.5%。

这不是一次普通的"自研芯片秀肌肉"，而是大厂算力主权叙事的一次关键转向。行业惯例是一到两年迭代一代AI芯片，Meta用模块化chiplet把周期压到半年，本质是把芯片开发从"押注下一代"变成"滚动小步快跑"，用工程组织的敏捷去对冲"模型演进快于芯片代际"的结构性矛盾。更值得警惕的是它的"推理优先"哲学：传统大厂先做训练芯片再向下适配推理，Meta反其道——450与500专为生成式AI推理优化，直接对准HBM带宽这个推理最痛的瓶颈。这是算力竞争从"谁训练得快"转向"谁serving得便宜"的明确信号。

对英伟达而言，MTIA目前只做推理、不对外销售，短期不构成直接替代，但Meta是全球最大的推理负载方之一（数十亿用户的推荐、广告与AI助手），把这部分从H200迁移到自研硅，等于在英伟达毛利最厚的推理市场切走一块。第三方测算MTIA 400约6 PFLOPs FP8、288GB HBM、9.2TB/s带宽，已超H200的4 PFLOPs/141GB/3.35TB/s，尤其内存容量翻倍利于免模型并行地服务大模型。对Meta自身，推理占总运营成本大头，自研ASIC可显著摊薄边际成本，直接撑住Llama API的低价策略，复制谷歌用TPU压低Gemini API定价的路径。对博通，再锁五年长约加1GW起步承诺，定制芯片已成其在英伟达之外的"隐形冠军"赛道。

未来3到12个月值得盯三个信号：一是Meta推理机队中自研硅占比是否在2026年底明显抬升；二是MTIA 450（计划2027年初量产）的HBM带宽能否真落地到18.4TB/s量级；三是苹果、亚马逊、微软是否加速各自推理ASIC以对冲。预判（推测）：若2027年上半年Meta自研芯片承接了其新增GenAI推理负载的30%以上、且单位token成本较H200方案下降超20%，则可证伪"自研ASIC只是训练补充"的旧叙事，标志大厂推理层"去英伟达化"从口号进入规模替代期。

我们认为，Meta这步棋的真正看点不在单颗芯片跑分，而在"节奏加定位"的组合打法。把发布周期压到半年，是用敏捷工程去消化模型与硬件之间的速度差；把first priority押在推理而非训练，是看清未来十年成本主战场是serving而非training。但风险同样清晰：MTIA不对外、生态封闭，一旦模型架构出现非预期突变，沉没的NRE与产线切换成本极高；而训练侧它仍深度依赖英伟达与AMD，所谓"硅主权"目前只是半场主权。这场豪赌的胜负，最终要看2027年那颗450芯片能否在真实流量里把账算平。

Meta.title: Meta AI Features Guide: How to Use the Assistant
Meta.description: Meta AI is Meta’s assistant for asking questions, getting help with ideas, and creating or editing images in supported products. ... The main Meta AI features are conversational answers, idea generation, help with writing, image generation and editing, and, in some experiences, voice interaction and web-assisted answers.
Meta.content:
- November 4, 2026

Meta AI is Meta’s assistant for asking questions, getting help with ideas, and creating or editing images in supported products. People can reach it through the standalone app and web experience, as well as features inside apps such as WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, and Messenger, though the available tools differ by app and account. For a useful result, treat it as a fast first draft or research starting point, then check facts that matter before acting on them.

The name covers more than one interaction. A text chat, a voice conversation, an image-generation prompt, and an assistant in a group chat can all behave differently. That matters when you are choosing where to use it and what information to share.

#### What Meta AI features can help with

The main Meta AI features are conversational answers, idea generation, help with writing, image generation and editing, and, in some experiences, voice interaction and web-assisted answers. Meta’s standalone app announcement describes text and voice conversations, image creation and editing, a Discover feed, and an assistant that can use web search for questions and recommendations. Those tools can save time on the blank-page part of a task. They do not remove the need to check names, numbers, dates, and sources.

For everyday questions, Meta AI can give a plain explanation, a short comparison, or a list of points to verify. A useful prompt gives the assistant a little context: “Explain this invoice term in everyday language,” or “Give me three ways to structure a product announcement for existing customers.” If the first answer is too broad, narrow the audience, length, or format in a follow-up. The wording of the request often matters more than writing a long prompt.

A Meta AI chatbot can also help draft emails, organize notes, suggest meal ideas, explain a photo, or outline a trip. These are starting points, not verified outcomes. Check product specifications against the manufacturer, verify a quotation in the original document, and confirm any changing fact with an up-to-date source. A confident answer can still be wrong, especially when the prompt leaves out important context.

In some experiences, Meta AI may personalize replies based on details a person has chosen to share or account context available there. Meta has described memory and personalization features in its app, while its WhatsApp help pages explain that account information may be used in some cases to tailor answers. Look at the in-app controls before relying on memory, and avoid assuming the same personalization settings apply across every product.

#### How to use Meta AI for everyday tasks

If you searched for how to use Meta AI, the practical answer is simple: open a supported Meta AI surface, state the task, include the context that changes the answer, and review the result. Depending on your account, that surface may be the standalone app, the web interface, or an entry point within another Meta app. The assistant’s icon, tools, and availability can vary, so follow the instructions shown in the product you are using.

For a writing task, specify the reader and the job. “Rewrite this paragraph for a first-time customer, keep the product details unchanged, and use a calm tone” is more useful than “make this better.” For planning, include constraints such as time, budget, dietary needs, or equipment. For explanations, say what you already understand and where you get stuck. A little context can prevent a string of generic follow-ups.

Do not paste an entire contract or client database just because the chat box accepts it. Remove names, account numbers, private messages, and other details the assistant does not need. Meta says prompts and messages deliberately shared with its AI can be received and used to provide responses, and may also help improve AI quality. Check the privacy information and available controls in the relevant app before sharing material you would not post elsewhere.

If the answer includes a source or link, open it. A cited page may support one part of the response but not every claim around it. When the topic involves a current price, an account policy, or a technical requirement, look for the original documentation and compare the date. This extra step is worthwhile when someone will spend money or make a business decision based on the answer.

#### Create and revise images with the Meta AI image generator

The Meta AI image generator can create images from text prompts and support edits in experiences where the tool is available. Meta’s Muse Image announcement describes prompt-based image creation and editing, suggested presets, and options for changing a picture’s style or appearance. The exact controls can change as the product rolls out, so check the version in your app rather than relying on a tutorial recorded months earlier.

A clear prompt describes the subject, setting, composition, visual style, and anything that must stay out of the image. “A small ceramic desk lamp on a pale wooden table, viewed from above, editorial product photograph, no text or logos” gives more direction than “make a nice lamp picture.” If you are editing an existing image, say what to change and what to preserve. For example, ask for a different background while keeping the product shape and label untouched.

Use short follow-ups to adjust one thing at a time. Ask to widen the crop, soften the lighting, or remove a distracting object. If every revision changes several details, it becomes hard to tell which instruction caused the result. For a brand asset, inspect the output for misspelled text, distorted products, and visual details that could mislead a customer. Do not treat generated packaging, logos, charts, or product screenshots as accurate unless they have been checked.

Before publishing, review rights and disclosure requirements that apply to the project. Keep the original source image and the final prompt with the work files. That makes later edits easier and gives the team a record of how the asset was created. Meta’s 2026 announcement also described image outputs that people can download and share, but availability and workflow details may differ across its products.

#### Using Meta AI on WhatsApp without confusing it with private chats

Meta AI on WhatsApp can be used in a direct interaction, in some existing group chats when someone mentions @Meta AI, or by sharing a message with the assistant. WhatsApp’s help center also lists questions, recommendations, ideas, and AI-generated images among possible uses. The assistant does not read every personal conversation simply because it is available in the app. WhatsApp says Meta can read messages that mention @Meta AI or that a person chooses to share with it; other personal messages and calls remain end-to-end encrypted.

That distinction is useful, but it is not a reason to share sensitive information. A prompt sent to the assistant is different from an ordinary private message to a contact. Avoid sharing health records, passwords, financial details, confidential work, or another person’s private information unless you have a clear reason and have reviewed the applicable controls. WhatsApp also says people can delete individual AI chats or request deletion of information they previously shared with Meta AI.

In a group, think about the social setting before inviting the assistant into the conversation. A short request for a definition may be fine; asking it to summarize a private disagreement can expose more context than the group intended to share. The group members should know when a prompt or message is being sent to an AI service. If the assistant’s answer includes a link, open the page and check whether it supports the response.

#### Where access and answers can differ

A feature shown in a product announcement may not appear for every person at the same time. Meta and WhatsApp both note that availability can vary by product, account, location, or device language. The assistant may also show different tools depending on whether you use the app, browser, or a chat integration. If an option is missing, check the app version and current help page before concluding that the feature has been removed.

Treat answers as drafts when the stakes are high. The assistant can misread a question, make up a detail, or produce an outdated explanation. Ask it to show sources when available, then verify those sources yourself. Do not rely on a generated answer alone for medical, legal, financial, safety, or employment decisions.

The same caution applies to images. A generated image can look plausible while containing a false label, a broken interface, or an object with the wrong proportions. Use it for ideation or a draft visual, then have someone inspect it before it represents a real product, service, or event. The more a viewer could mistake the image for documentary evidence, the more carefully it needs to be checked.

#### FAQs

##### What is Meta AI used for?

Meta AI can answer questions, explain topics, help generate ideas, draft or revise text, and create or edit images in supported experiences. The specific tools depend on the product and account, and answers should be checked before you rely on them.

##### Is Meta AI on WhatsApp private?

WhatsApp says personal messages and calls remain end-to-end encrypted. Messages that mention @Meta AI or that you choose to share with the assistant can be read by Meta to provide a response; unrelated personal messages are not readable by Meta. Avoid sending sensitive information unless you have reviewed the relevant privacy details

##### Can the Meta AI image generator edit an existing picture?

In supported experiences, it can create images and help edit them using text instructions or presets. Describe the requested change and what must remain unchanged, then check the result for errors before sharing or using it commercially.

# 乌镇奏响开源开放协奏曲

“为什么要开源？答案非常简单，为了AGI(通用人工智能)更快到来。”

11月3日，深度求索(DeepSeek)研究工程师高熙在2026世界互联网大会乌镇峰会“人工智能乌镇对话”中，回应了DeepSeek开源逻辑。

AGI被视为人工智能发展的终极目标之一，代表在任何认知任务上达到或超越人类水平的人工智能系统。“如果说AGI本来要10年才到来，我会希望在一年后到，如果AGI本来是一年到来，那我希望明天就到。”高熙这番话，道出了希望通过开源加快AI发展的初衷。

DeepSeek可谓是开源的急先锋。近期，其宣布将内部推理框架DeepInfer全面开源。开源的选择，也成就了DeepSeek。全球AI模型聚合平台OpenRouter数据显示，10月19日到25日，DeepSeek登顶全球第一。

德国明斯特大学教授Bernd Holznagel对三里河表示，现在硅谷许多公司及德国40%-50%的中小企业都在使用中国的开源大模型。“我也用过DeepSeek，很好用。”

开源是中国大模型的鲜明标志。阿里巴巴集团联合创始人、董事会主席蔡崇信表示，中国同仁们在AI发展上不约而同地选择开源，是来自中国创新的重要精神内核。AI只有开源才能普及，只有普及才能创造可持续、普惠的智能时代。

在阿里巴巴ATH事业群千问大语言模型项目负责人刘大一恒看来，开源改变了AI创新的范式，使核心技术不再仅掌握在少数企业手中，而是让全球开发者和生态共同参与创新。而且，开源模型的存在将模型性价比拉升至较高区间，避免了闭源模型可能出现的价格垄断，降低了大众使用门槛。

但不可否认的是，开源模型同样具有风险，如何在开源开放中维护安全可信、在共建共享中缩小发展差距，成为全球重大挑战。

安全不是某一家公司、某一个国家独自扛下的担子。“安全这件事不能听天由命，不能只靠少数顶尖学者或者一小群人，必须建立一套成型的机制。”国际人工智能治理协会主席约翰·希金斯表示，在开源体系下，安全责任由大家共同分担，因此共同体建设尤为关键。

今年乌镇峰会的主题，正是“开源开放 共建共享——携手构建网络空间命运共同体”。

呼应全球关切，峰会期间发布的《携手构建全球开放人工智能行动倡议》，围绕共同推进开放和发展、共同维护安全和可信、共同参与对话和治理、共同坚持互利和包容四个方面，提出18条具体行动倡议。

它传递的信号很明确，AI 不是单打独斗的赛场，需要共商共建共享的治理思路，一起搭建公平可信、可持续的智能生态。

说到底，乌镇这场关于开源的讨论，回答的不只是一家企业的技术路线，更是AI 时代我们想走一条什么样的路。

AI 这条路，有两种走法，一种是攥紧技术、关起门独享红利；另一种是打开大门，汇聚全世界的智慧一起往前走。开源，选的是后者。

现实已表明，垒起“小院高墙”、构筑“数字铁幕”的封闭生态，难以独立支撑全球公平普惠发展。尽管开源的前路还有不少难题，但已是人心所向、大势所趋。

DeepSeek.title: 乌镇对“数字铁幕”说不
DeepSeek.description: 11月3日，深度求索（DeepSeek）研究工程师高熙在2026世界互联网大会乌镇峰会“人工智能乌镇对话”中，回应了DeepSeek开源逻辑 ... DeepSeek可谓是开源的急先锋。近期，其宣布将内部推理框架DeepInfer全面开源。开源的选择，也成就了DeepSeek。
DeepSeek.content:
## 新浪科技

# 乌镇对“数字铁幕”说不

乌镇给出答案。

“为什么要开源？答案非常简单，为了AGI（通用人工智能）更快到来。”

11月3日，深度求索（DeepSeek）研究工程师高熙在2026世界互联网大会乌镇峰会“人工智能乌镇对话”中，回应了DeepSeek开源逻辑。

AGI被视为人工智能发展的终极目标之一，代表在任何认知任务上达到或超越人类水平的人工智能系统。“如果说AGI本来要10年才到来，我会希望在一年后到，如果AGI本来是一年到来，那我希望明天就到。”高熙这番话，道出了希望通过开源加快AI发展的初衷。

DeepSeek可谓是开源的急先锋。近期，其宣布将内部推理框架DeepInfer全面开源。开源的选择，也成就了DeepSeek。全球AI模型聚合平台OpenRouter数据显示，10月19日到25日，DeepSeek登顶全球第一。

德国明斯特大学教授Bernd Holznagel对三里河表示，现在硅谷许多公司及德国40%-50%的中小企业都在使用中国的开源大模型。“我也用过DeepSeek，很好用。”

开源是中国大模型的鲜明标志。阿里巴巴集团联合创始人、董事会主席蔡崇信表示，中国同仁们在AI发展上不约而同地选择开源，是来自中国创新的重要精神内核。AI只有开源才能普及，只有普及才能创造可持续、普惠的智能时代。

在阿里巴巴ATH事业群千问大语言模型项目负责人刘大一恒看来，开源改变了AI创新的范式，使核心技术不再仅掌握在少数企业手中，而是让全球开发者和生态共同参与创新。而且，开源模型的存在将模型性价比拉升至较高区间，避免了闭源模型可能出现的价格垄断，降低了大众使用门槛。

但不可否认的是，开源模型同样具有风险，如何在开源开放中维护安全可信、在共建共享中缩小发展差距，成为全球重大挑战。

安全不是某一家公司、某一个国家独自扛下的担子。“安全这件事不能听天由命，不能只靠少数顶尖学者或者一小群人，必须建立一套成型的机制。”国际人工智能治理协会主席约翰·希金斯表示，在开源体系下，安全责任由大家共同分担，因此共同体建设尤为关键。

今年乌镇峰会的主题，正是“开源开放 共建共享——携手构建网络空间命运共同体”。

呼应全球关切，峰会期间发布的《携手构建全球开放人工智能行动倡议》，围绕共同推进开放和发展、共同维护安全和可信、共同参与对话和治理、共同坚持互利和包容四个方面，提出18条具体行动倡议。

它传递的信号很明确，AI 不是单打独斗的赛场，需要共商共建共享的治理思路，一起搭建公平可信、可持续的智能生态。

说到底，乌镇这场关于开源的讨论，回答的不只是一家企业的技术路线，更是AI 时代我们想走一条什么样的路。

AI 这条路，有两种走法，一种是攥紧技术、关起门独享红利；另一种是打开大门，汇聚全世界的智慧一起往前走。开源，选的是后者。

现实已表明，垒起“小院高墙”、构筑“数字铁幕”的封闭生态，难以独立支撑全球公平普惠发展。尽管开源的前路还有不少难题，但已是人心所向、大势所趋。

｜策划：周锐

｜统筹：王庆凯

｜执笔：李金磊

DeepSeek.content:

# DeepSeek wants to steal Claude Code and Codex’s lunch with an AI Super Agent that does not wait around

The AI coding race is moving beyond chatbots that write code when developers prompt them to. DeepSeek wants its next agent to be a little more aggressive. The Chinese AI company has released a prototype called Super-Agent, an open-source coding tool that listens in on developer group chats, identifies coding problems, and suggests solutions without waiting to be called.

The move puts DeepSeek in more direct competition with Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex, two prominent names in the rapidly-growing market for AI-powered software development. The bigger goal is clear: to design AI agents to be less assistants waiting for instructions, and more members of a development team who can take initiative.

## DeepSeek's coding agents are going to stop waiting for prompts

DeepSeek's Harness team has launched Super-Agent, which is designed to scan developer discussions for feedback on coding problems and recommend possible solutions. The company says its goal is to provide the maximum value with the minimum human attention.

Advertisement

Advertisement

That's a significant departure from the familiar chatbot workflow. Typically, developers describe a problem, provide some context, and then ask the AI tool to write or fix code. DeepSeek's approach attempts to bring the agent closer to the conversations where those problems originate in the first place.

The technology behind this is called the agent harness, a software scaffolding that wraps around a large language model and equips it with the tools to take on more complex tasks. DeepSeek set up its Harness team earlier this year to build agents that can provide the coding services of leading US AI firms.

But this is a prototype, not proof that DeepSeek has already surpassed established rivals. The announcement doesn't set the bar for how reliable Super-Agent is for complex development work, or how ready it is for deployment at scale.

## Claude Code and OpenAI Codex have serious competition to keep an eye on

Anthropic's Claude Code is already helping developers navigate codebases, debug issues, write code, run tests, and make pull requests. And not just code, but agent-based workflows across software development, including parallel tasks and tools for reviewing code, have been demonstrated by Codex at OpenAI.

Advertisement

Advertisement

Now DeepSeek is moving into similar territory, but Super-Agent gets an interesting angle by focusing on proactively monitoring developer conversations. Rather than simply answering a developer's question, it tries to figure out when a developer might need help.

This is important because the next phase of AI competition is increasingly about agents that can automate entire chunks of work, not just generate impressive answers. OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek are all pursuing that opportunity.

DeepSeek is also getting ready for a big financial push. In its latest fundraising round ahead of a planned initial public offering, the company has raised about 100 billion yuan ($15 billion), Bloomberg reported.

More competition could eventually lead to more capable and affordable coding tools for developers. But for now, Super-Agent is an early sign of the direction the industry is going – not a reason to uninstall Claude Code or Codex just yet.

DeepSeek.title: DeepSeek发布创作者模式
DeepSeek.description: 此前澎湃新闻记者确认到，DeepSeek下一代大模型DeepSeek V5计划基于华为昇腾芯片进行预训练。此前华为昇腾芯片主要用于DeepSeek大模型的推理任务，V5将是其首款原生依托昇腾950开展训练的大模型。
DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek发布创作者模式

澎湃新闻消息，“你的Harness，由你定义。”（Your Harness. You Define It）在发布智能体更新后，DeepSeek再次更新Creator Mode（创作者模式）。

11月2日，澎湃新闻记者获悉，DeepSeek Harness发布Creator Mode（创作者模式）演示视频，集中展示通过对话创建插件的能力，并公开七组演示的中英文提示词。

据DeepSeek在推送中介绍：“来认识DeepSeek Harness中的‘创造模式’，把想法转化为你能直接使用的插件：可以是设计工作台、沙盒游戏，或是一个3D大模型可视化工具，你会创造出什么？”

所谓Harness，是指围绕大语言模型构建的一套软件支撑框架，旨在帮助AI Agent管理和执行更加复杂的任务。简单来说，它可以被理解为让一个大模型真正成为Agent所需要的整套运行系统。

具体而言，此次展示的Creator Mode，是让用户通过对话创建自己的工具和界面。用户切换到Creator mode，在输入框里描述需求后就能打开插件，不同颜色的便签排列在画面里。输入内容、选择颜色，就能把想法添加到墙上，生成的插件可以从侧栏或会话中打开，以独立面板呈现。这也体现Harness“一切皆插件”的设计：通过安装或创建插件，扩展工具、技能和界面。

通俗来说，此次更新的创造模式，指的是用户口头描述一个需求，系统就能把它写成一个即插即用、可在桌面端运行的插件，典型例子正是文中提到的设计工作台、沙盒游戏、3D LLM可视化工具等。

此次展示进一步扩展DeepSeek Harness的使用场景：用户可通过对话创建插件，将设计、剪辑、阅读等工具接入日常工作，并按需调整应用界面。

此前澎湃新闻记者确认到，DeepSeek下一代大模型DeepSeek V5计划基于华为昇腾芯片进行预训练。此前华为昇腾芯片主要用于DeepSeek大模型的推理任务，V5将是其首款原生依托昇腾950开展训练的大模型。华为昇腾950系列分为950PR与950DT两款芯片，均基于第三代达芬奇架构，主要面向大模型的训练与推理场景。

10月31日，DeepSeekHarness团队在官方公众号发表技术文章《Super-agent设计探索：迈向更自主的Agent系统》。

DeepSeek表示，模型能力提升催生了新的应用形态，个人助手（Personal Agent）开始集中涌现。它们直接接入日常的消息、日程、邮件与工作平台，持续观察信息流并协助处理事务。这种持续在线、事件驱动的工作模式并不局限于个人场景，个人助手只是其中一类应用；在软件开发等商业场景中，它同样很有价值。

然而，现有主流Agent设计还难以在多任务和团队协作的规模上支撑这一模式，多任务上限取决于人的注意力。

Agent的工作模式仍然以单一Session为基本单位，不同Session之间彼此独立。当用户并行推进多项工作时，必须手动切换并记住各个Session的上下文，而据团队观察，一个人通常只能同时跟进3到5个活跃Session。在这种设计下，单任务的上限取决于模型能力，多任务的上限取决于人的注意力。

DeepSeek团队通过双层架构、事件驱动、异步多信道交互、存算分离与外部Watchdog，系统在底层接管了繁琐的会话管理与上下文同步，使人类得以从具体的执行细节进一步上移到更高层的决策与验收。DeepSeek把这种Agent形态及其系统架构称为Super-agent。

原标题：DeepSeek发布创作者模式，下一代大模型计划基于华为昇腾芯片预训练

DeepSeek.content:
旗下矩阵

- 投资界AI

# 实测 DeepSeek 「创造模式」

从10月开始，DeepSeek接连放出多款产品。从和V4.1 Flash 1017同步上线的搜索服务，再到开源了自家线上在用的推理框架DeepInfer、编解码组件deepseek-recipe。10月底，DSH又开源了Super Agent原型。

作者：苗正 编辑 王靖 来源：微信公众号：字母榜 更新于： 阅读约5分钟 2812字

11月2日晚上，DSH官方在社交媒体上发了文称“你的Harness，你来定义”，同时发布了DSH的创造模式，并配了一支1分39秒的视频来介绍创造模式。

这个创造模式指的是让用户用自然语言描述一个想法，由Agent自己写代码、打包，并把它安装成DSH里能直接用的插件。

DeepSeek官方放出了7个演示，包括3D Transformer可视化、带多轨时间线的视频剪辑台、保留原版式的论文阅读器、海报设计工作台、3D 地标馆、能把整个界面换成像素风的主题插件，以及统计token和成本的用量仪表盘。

DeepSeek官方同时公开了这7个演示的中英文提示词，复制进去、选中创造模式就能复现。

严格说，这个模式并不是新东西。AI科技评论博主罗汉·保罗（Rohan Paul）表示，DSH的创造模式从8月开始就已经有了，11月2日新发的是演示视频和提示词。

其实早在10月2日Claude Code推出Mods功能时，崔添翼就发文表示庆祝，同时简单介绍了DSH创造模式的几大特点。比如用来改界面、改Agent循环机制，或增加新的编排方式。

所以这次发布的意义，更像是把一项潜伏已久的能力，以“创造模式”的身份单拎出来。

社区在经过测试之后，给了DSH创造模式“特别好评”。

比如中文区博主@NFT_Chen当天拿官方提示词实测了一轮，称3个插件都跑通了，3D地标馆约21分钟、花费0.38美元，海报工作台约10分钟、0.1美元，会话统计约11分钟、0.16美元。安装前会弹窗询问权限，点“允许一次”即可。

不过也有用户表示，创造模式还有改进的空间。

目前创造模式的运行逻辑是，Agent写完代码后会直接安装这个插件，所以如果Agent写的代码有bug，或者被恶意提示词诱导写了对电脑有危害的东西，那么就会对用户的电脑造成损害。

这个担忧本身是必要的，创造模式生成的是可执行插件，权限和代码安全本来就是问题，DeepSeek自己也承认，部分演示需要多轮打磨，且整个项目仍处于开发者预览阶段，核心插件和API可能出现破坏性变更。

科技媒体Startup Fortune认为，DeepSeek是在放大开源的优势。

创造模式和发布模型的逻辑是逆着来的，发布模型是AI厂商有什么技术，就往模型里塞什么技术。但是创造模式是使用者先提需求，然后再得到产品。供需关系刚好相反。

DeepSeek给出了DSH的骨架，用户和社区决定了DSH的样子。DSH的特点是一切皆为插件，它的界面是插件，工具也是插件。比起给DSH开发插件，倒不如直接让用户自己定义插件。

这样一来，使用者就会替DeepSeek造真正有需求的插件，然后DeepSeek可以通过插件市场的方式，上架这些产品。

通过创造模式，DeepSeek将开源普惠的市场策略，落地成了一种开发者生态。

创造模式所反映的，也正是DeepSeek目前的状态，把定义权交到开发者手里。

从10月开始，DeepSeek接连放出多款产品。从和V4.1 Flash 1017同步上线的搜索服务，再到开源了自家线上在用的推理框架DeepInfer、编解码组件deepseek-recipe。10月底，DSH又开源了Super Agent原型。

从底层模型到上层Agent，DeepSeek几乎每一层都在往外递。但“定义权”到底好不好用，光看官方演示和别人的测试还不够，我也亲自上手，用创造模式做了两个插件。

实测

创造模式的提示词逻辑和DeepSeek在V4.1 Flash 1017中提到的许愿式编程差不多，你不用描述这个插件具体要怎样，只需要描述你想要的最终成果就可以了。

不过话又说回来了，描述得越详细，这个插件的效果就越好。

DSH官方示例中，创造模式可以生成3D预览，还可以开发游戏。于是我将两者结合，选择创造模式后，仿照官方示例，给出以下提示词。

“创建一个带左侧边栏入口的DeepSeek Harness插件，做成可交互的3D演示游戏，用鲸鱼娘的形象搞个3D版马里奥。”

虽然鲸鱼娘的形象有点惨不忍睹，但是游戏质量很好，操作手感也很还原FC版本的马里奥。

从输入提示词开始算起，整个开发过程时间为1小时14分钟。

有了这次的经验，接下来我在使用创造模式的时候，会专门给DeepSeek找一些图片素材，让它能生成更符合大众审美的内容。

第二个提示词如下。

这个桌面宠物不仅可以互动，还能根据我和DeepSeek的聊天，给出一些有趣的反应。正如视频里所展示的那样，输入提示词之后，鲸鱼娘桌面宠物会提示DeepSeek正在思考。

当DeepSeek给出答案后，鲸鱼娘还会说“这一轮写完啦。要不要摸摸我，当作休息一下？”

但是这还没完，因为除了基本的互动外，DeepSeek还给这个鲸鱼娘三个属性，分别为“羁绊”、“心情”、“元气”。可以通过对话和交互提升这些属性，属性越高鲸鱼娘越开心，越低则会出现疲惫的情况，比如她会提示她累了，需要休息。

两个插件的提示词加一块也才100个字，许愿式编程还是太权威了。

不过在生成过程中需要多次点击“允许”，并没有像社区说的那样，可以点一次就不管了。即使我用了DSH的实验性自动审查插件，依然需要点很多次“允许”。

此外，这两个插件的开发过程中，DSH的缓存命中都是99%。两个插件加一块，总费用约为6块钱。

说起模型开发游戏，就不得不提Anthropic。

《大海捞针模拟器》的开发者在发布游戏试玩版后，其游戏被多位开发者使用Claude克隆后抢先上架，导致原版的《大海捞针模拟器》反而成了“仿品”。这位开发者甚至还收到勒索邮件，不少工作室因此取消了公开试玩。

10月底，Claude给用户发送通知，原文大意是：可以做原创游戏、某一类型的游戏、基于用户自己设计和素材的游戏，但不要复刻某款特定的现有游戏，即使改了名字或自称原创。

随后Anthropic工程师艾迪·奥斯马尼（Addy Osmani）表示情况属实，Anthropic在Opus 5.5运行Claude Code时，会给系统提示词加这么两句话，以防止用户在使用Claude时，侵犯知识产权、违反使用规则。

回到创造模式本身，即便还有权限确认繁琐、生成素材审美不稳定这类小问题，但是它拉低插件开发门槛的效果是实打实的。

创造模式刚好填上了 “脑子里的小想法” 和 “工具” 之间的空白。想到什么，或者发现什么问题，直接说给DSH的创造模式，让它来帮你解决。

还有一点，目前为止，DSH没有官方的插件市场。仅提供了“自定义插件索引源”的底层机制。

用户可以在设置中开启实验性的自定义插件市场功能，手动添加第三方维护的索引地址，实现插件的浏览、搜索与一键安装。

DeepSeek官方也没有官方统一的插件分发平台。

有了创造模式，民间大神们难免会跑出高频实用爆款插件，这可能也会倒逼DSH开插件市场。

无论如何，至少对普通用户来说，现在随手就能给自己的DSH定制点专属小功能，这件事本身就足够有新鲜感。

# 玩转 Vibe Coding！Qwen3.7-Plus 看图写代码原理、缓存策略、Token Plan 计费全流程

2026-11-04 20

举报

简介： 开发者上线业务之前，要完整理解阶梯按量计费、Token Plan订阅、NightPlan夜间错峰、上下文缓存计费规则，认清Plus与Max、Flash之间的能力边界，注意控制单次输入Token规模，避免触发高价计费档位。接入层面优先使用OpenAI兼容接口，便于对接主流开发框架；生产环境建议锁定快照版本，配置用量告警，增加异常捕获与重试逻辑。线上业务推荐分层路由策略，简单任务交给Flash处理，中等图文混合任务分发Qwen3.7‑Plus，高难度纯文本业务选用Qwen3.7‑Max，高难度多模态业务选用Qwen3.8‑Max，平衡业务输出质量与推理成本。正式上线前，使用真实业务数据集完成充分测

Qwen3.7‑Plus属于千问3.7系列均衡型多模态基座，兼顾文本深度推理、图文视频解析、Agent工具调用与工程代码生成能力，定位介于Qwen3.7‑Flash与Qwen3.7‑Max之间，原生支持文本、图片、长视频输入，百万Token超大上下文窗口，最大输出Token支持131072，深度思考模式最大思维链长度可达262144 Token，擅长混合模态智能体、GUI截图理解、Vibe Coding视觉辅助编程、中等难度长文档分析、图文知识库业务。很多开发者容易混淆Plus与Max、Flash之间的能力边界，把Plus用于超复杂深度推理任务，出现逻辑退化；也有大量开发者对阶梯式按量计费、Token Plan订阅、上下文缓存、夜间错峰权益理解模糊，业务上线后出现成本不可控。

本文完整拆解Qwen3.7‑Plus底层规格参数、全套核心能力、完整计费体系、接入配置流程、多语言调用代码示例、业务选型策略以及生产环境避坑要点，覆盖个人开发者原型验证、中小企业线上业务落地、企业混合模态智能工作流开发全流程。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

## 一、Qwen3.7‑Plus核心功能与硬件规格参数

### 1.1底层基础规格

模型调用ID固定为qwen3.7‑plus，快照版本为qwen3.7‑plus‑2026‑05‑26，正式生产业务强烈建议使用快照版本锁定模型能力，规避平台后台模型迭代带来输出效果漂移，测试环境可以直接使用通用ID跟随最新版本能力。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

关键规格参数：

- 整体上下文窗口：1000000 Token，支持超长文档、大量图文混合内容一次性载入
- 最大输入Token：991808，开启深度思考模式最大输入983616
- 最大输出Token：131072，深度思考模式最大思维链长度262144 Token
- 输入模态：文本、图片、长视频；输出仅支持文本，支持多图、多段视频混合传入
- 核心能力：Function Calling函数调用、强制结构化JSON输出、上下文缓存、内置代码解释器、网页检索工具、前缀续写
- 不支持自定义微调，国内地域支持批量推理，国际部署地域不开放批量推理能力
- 限流指标：国内区域RPM 20000，TPM每分钟300万Token；限流属于动态阈值，订阅档位提升，平台会自动上调调用限额
- 接口生态：完整兼容OpenAI兼容接口，可以无缝对接LangChain、LlamaIndex、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw等主流开发框架，适配混合模态智能体开发工作流。

### 1.2核心能力拆解

深度推理与深度思考模式
Qwen3.7‑Plus具备较强文本推理能力，开启enable_thinking参数后输出完整内部思考链路，面对中等难度数学推导、业务方案拆解、合同初步分析，推理质量大幅提升。开启思考模式会额外消耗大量输出Token，拉高整体计费开销；普通问答、图文摘要业务建议关闭深度思考，复杂任务按需开启。对比Qwen3.7‑Max纯文本旗舰，Plus在极高难度纯文本推演上存在差距；对比Flash系列，推理稳定性、长文档召回能力明显更强。

Vibe Coding视觉辅助代码生成能力
这是Plus非常核心的差异化能力，可以读取UI界面截图，识别页面布局、组件样式，直接输出前端业务代码，实现截图转页面，适配前端开发辅助场景。同时支持后端脚本、业务模块、算法代码编写，能够完成中小型软件项目迭代开发；大型完整工程、多文件深度重构，能力距离Max旗舰存在明显上限。

混合模态Agent智能体与工具调用
完整支持Function Calling函数调用，支持文本+截图混合输入的智能体工作流，可以读取GUI界面截图，结合工具调用完成业务规划，适配轻量视觉Agent场景。支持多轮工具循环调用，自主规划任务、调用外部工具、依据返回结果纠错迭代。当工具调用轮次过多、任务逻辑极度复杂时，JSON格式出错概率会上升，业务代码依旧需要增加JSON解析异常捕获、重试降级逻辑。适合中等复杂度图文混合自动化工作流，几十轮超长循环高难度Agent建议选用Max系列。

原生多模态图文视频解析能力
原生支持图片、长视频输入，能够解析复杂图表、扫描文档PDF截图、软件操作界面、长时间视频内容，提取图表数据、总结视频关键业务信息，识别界面按钮布局，适合图文知识库、截图分析、视频内容摘要、GUI操作智能体业务。图片支持高分辨率大图解析，视频输入存在时长与文件大小限制，超长视频业务需要提前分片预处理；内网图片视频资源必须开启公网访问权限，否则模型无法拉取资源，直接返回请求异常。

百万Token长文档处理能力
百万级上下文窗口，支持一次性载入几十万字合同、研报、项目文档，完成文档归纳、风险点提取、内容对比。相较于Flash，Plus超长文档远端信息召回能力更强；面对几十万字超深度逻辑推演，表现弱于Max旗舰，超大规模复杂文档建议做分片预处理。

上下文缓存能力
完整支持隐式自动缓存、显式标记缓存两种模式，针对固定不变的system系统提示词、知识库公共前缀做缓存，缓存命中之后输入Token计费大幅下降，同时降低接口响应延迟。在Agent循环对话、图文知识库问答业务收益巨大；如果每轮请求全部内容动态变化，缓存很难命中，开启缓存反而带来缓存创建的额外开销。

结构化输出与内置工具集
原生支持强制JSON结构化输出，降低JSON解析失败概率；内置代码解释器、网页抓取、联网检索工具，不需要额外开发，即可完成网页内容读取、代码运行、资料检索，降低混合模态智能体业务开发成本。

## 二、计费体系：按量计费、Token Plan订阅、夜间错峰权益、上下文缓存完整规则

Qwen3.7‑Plus包含按量后付费、Token Plan个人版订阅、Token Plan团队版订阅三套计费模式，支持上下文缓存折扣，同时支持NightPlan夜间错峰折扣权益，面向已经开通Token Plan订阅的客户，北京时间22:00‑次日8:00享受错峰优惠，适合离线批量图文文档处理、异步非实时任务。该模型按量计费为阶梯定价，单次请求输入Token不同，单价会发生变化，开发者需要区分不同抵扣逻辑，避免线上账单失控。

### 2.1按量计费（原价模式）

按量计费按照输入Token、输出Token分开统计计费，分为两个阶梯：单次输入≤256k Token、256k＜单次输入≤1M Token，缓存命中输入会执行折扣计价，国内区域原价参考如下，实际结算价格以百炼控制台账单明细为准：

单次输入≤256k Token
- 普通输入Token：2元 / 每百万tokens
- 普通输出Token：8元 / 每百万tokens
- 隐式缓存命中输入：0.4元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存创建：2.5元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存命中读取：0.2元 / 每百万tokens

256k＜单次输入≤1M Token
- 普通输入Token：6元 / 每百万tokens
- 普通输出Token：24元 / 每百万tokens
- 隐式缓存命中输入：1.2元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存创建：7.5元 / 每百万tokens
- 显式缓存命中读取：0.6元 / 每百万tokens

重要提示：开启enable_thinking深度思考，模型输出的思维链内容全部计入输出Token统计，会产生计费消耗；快照版本调用会附带少量额外输入Token，成本测算阶段需要纳入该损耗。百炼新用户会赠送一定免费测试额度，拥有90天有效期，适合前期POC验证使用。

### 2.2 Token Plan订阅（个人版与团队版）

Token Plan是预购Credits额度的订阅模式，购买Credits额度之后调用Qwen3.7‑Plus优先消耗订阅Credits，对比按量原价具备明显折扣，适合日均请求稳定、持续调用的业务场景。

- 个人版Token Plan：面向个人开发者，API Key仅限本人使用，禁止密钥对外共享，同一实名认证主体限购一份个人套餐；额度仅限当前账号，不支持拆分给多个子账号。
- 团队版Token Plan：面向企业业务场景，支持团队多子账号共享Credits额度，支持用量统计、成员权限管控，适合企业多条业务线同时调用模型。
- 抵扣规则：请求优先消耗订阅Credits，Credits全部耗尽之后，业务不会直接报错阻断，会自动切换为按量计费模式。开发者必须配置用量告警阈值，监控Credits消耗，防止额度耗尽之后按量产生高额账单。
- 套餐额度拥有固定有效期，过期未消耗Credits直接失效，需要结合业务预估Token消耗量选择档位，不要盲目采购大额套餐。
- NightPlan夜间错峰权益，仅对已经开通Token Plan订阅的账号生效，离线批量图文文档处理可以错峰夜间运行，降低推理成本；面向终端用户的实时在线业务不建议完全依赖夜间折扣。

### 2.3上下文缓存计费规则

缓存分为隐式自动缓存、显式标记缓存两种模式。隐式缓存系统自动识别公共请求前缀；显式缓存通过cache_control标记指定消息片段，缓存命中率更加可控。缓存创建阶段会产生溢价，后续多次读取享受极低单价。
当系统提示词、知识库公共前缀在大量请求中重复复用，缓存可以大幅降低成本；每轮请求内容全部动态变化，缓存几乎无法命中，此时开启缓存不会带来收益，反而增加缓存创建开销。判断缓存是否真正生效，不要只看API返回参数，以百炼控制台账单缓存计费明细作为结算依据。

### 2.4计费避坑重点

- 输入输出分开计费，输出Token单价高于输入，深度思考模式会额外增加输出Token消耗，普通业务关闭enable_thinking。
- Credits耗尽自动切换按量计费，不会阻断业务，务必配置用量告警。
- Qwen3.7‑Plus是阶梯计费，输入超过256k Token单价会大幅上涨，长文档业务尽量做分片，控制单次输入规模。
- NightPlan权益仅夜间时段生效，需要开通Token Plan订阅才可以享受，实时在线业务不可依赖该折扣。
- 缓存不是万能优化手段，业务请求内容频繁变动场景，关闭缓存避免额外开销。
- 快照版本会附加少量额外输入Token，成本测算需要计入损耗。

## 三、Qwen3.7‑Plus完整接入配置流程

接入分为DashScope原生SDK、OpenAI兼容接口两种，优先推荐OpenAI兼容接口，生态适配更好，可以直接对接LangChain、LlamaIndex、OpenClaw等主流开发工具。
接入前置准备步骤：

- 登录百炼控制台，创建API‑Key，妥善保存密钥，禁止硬编码写入业务代码，全部通过环境变量加载密钥。
- 在模型市场开通Qwen3.7‑Plus调用权限，快照版本需要手动开启访问权限。
- 确认账号具备按量余额，或者已经购买Token Plan订阅套餐。
- 测试环境完成接口调用、多模态图文视频解析、工具调用全量验证，再上线生产环境。

### 3.1 Python OpenAI兼容接口基础调用示例

import os
from openai import OpenAI
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()
client = OpenAI(
    api_key=os.getenv("DASHSCOPE_API_KEY"),
    base_url="https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1"
)

def qwen37plus_chat(user_query: str, enable_thinking: bool = False):
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="qwen3.7-plus",
        messages=[
            {
   "role":"system","content":"你是混合模态业务助手，回答严谨简洁。"},
            {
   "role":"user","content":user_query}
        ],
        extra_body={

            "enable_thinking": enable_thinking
        },
        max_tokens=8192,
        temperature=0.5,
        stream=False
    )
    usage_info = resp.usage
    print(f"输入token:{usage_info.prompt_tokens},输出token:{usage_info.completion_tokens}")
    return resp.choices[0].message.content

if __name__ == "__main__":
    result = qwen37plus_chat("梳理一份中小型Web前端项目开发方案，包含模块划分与风险评估", enable_thinking=False)
    print(result)

## 四、业务选型与适用场景

优先选择Qwen3.7‑Plus的场景

- 中等复杂度混合模态业务：图文知识库、截图解析、图表识别、短视频内容总结，兼顾推理质量与可控成本。
- Vibe Coding视觉辅助编程：读取UI截图生成前端代码，中小型Web项目开发辅助，前端代码助手。
- 中等复杂度混合模态Agent：文本+截图的轻量视觉智能体，多轮工具循环，GUI界面识别规划，不需要几十轮超长循环。
- 中等难度长文档处理：几十万字文档摘要、信息提取、对比归纳，非超深度逻辑推演场景。
- 离线批量图文处理：夜间批量截图解析、文档格式化，可利用NightPlan错峰折扣降低推理成本。
- 原型POC验证：混合模态项目前期快速验证业务流程，快速迭代调试，控制测试阶段Token消耗。

不建议直接选用该模型的场景

- 超高难度纯文本深度推理：复杂法律合同深度拆解、金融研报深度推演、大型完整软件工程重构，优先选择Qwen3.7‑Max。
- 高并发简单问答业务：大量普通闲聊、简单文本摘要，全部使用Plus会带来不必要成本，分层路由交由Flash处理。
- 几十轮超长循环复杂Agent：工具调用轮次极高，JSON出错概率上升，优先Max系列。

生产环境最佳实践是采用模型分层路由架构，简单请求分发Flash，中等图文混合任务使用Qwen3.7‑Plus，超高难度纯文本任务路由Qwen3.7‑Max，高难度多模态任务使用Qwen3.8‑Max，兼顾业务输出质量与整体推理成本。同时注意阶梯计费特性，单次输入尽量控制在256k Token以内，长文档做分片处理，避免触发高价档位。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

## 五、生产环境避坑与常见故障排查

开启深度思考带来成本上涨

enable_thinking开启后思维链全部计入输出Token，普通问答图文业务务必关闭，复杂任务按需开启，不要全局无条件打开思考模式。

密钥泄露风险

API Key禁止硬编码写进代码、提交代码仓库；个人版Token Plan密钥禁止对外共享，违规会被限制调用权限。

阶梯计费触发高价档位

Qwen3.7‑Plus为阶梯定价，单次输入Token超过256k，输入输出单价会明显上涨；长文档、大量图文输入业务，做好分片预处理，控制单次输入规模。

百万上下文不等于超强长文档推理

虽然支持百万Token输入，面对几十万Token文档做超深度逻辑推演，远端信息召回能力弱于Max系列，超大规模复杂文档建议分片。

多模态图片视频调用报错

图片、视频资源必须公网可访问，内网OSS资源需要开启外网访问权限；视频输入存在时长、文件大小上限，超长视频建议提前分片预处理。

工具调用JSON解析报错

Plus在多轮工具循环场景偶发JSON格式异常，业务代码必须增加JSON异常捕获、重试降级逻辑，不能完全信任模型输出格式。

缓存没有节省费用

业务每轮请求大部分内容动态变化，缓存命中率极低，应该关闭缓存；缓存收益主要来自固定不变的system提示词、知识库公共前缀。

快照版本选择
